title: Functional Decomposition and Function Map
definition: Functional decomposition divides a multi-step responsibility into named functions whose contracts form an inspectable function map.
purpose: Turn a large algorithm into understandable, testable steps without mechanically extracting every line.
history: Top-down functional decomposition is a longstanding structured-design technique; modern practice combines it with explicit contracts and iterative refactoring.
mental_model: Convert a journey into meaningful stages, then name each stage by its outcome rather than by incidental syntax.
analogy: A kitchen stations work toward one meal; useful for responsibilities, but software calls and data can branch or be reused in ways the kitchen analogy cannot model.
common_mistakes: Decomposing by syntax rather than responsibility
industry_notes: A function boundary should communicate a meaningful contract and change reason.
ai_notes: Require AI to produce a responsibility map before generating helper functions.
interview_notes: Ask how to choose function boundaries for a multi-step workflow.
